correctness.rationale: For the explicit five-row Latin square, full finite enumeration finds 56 reduced Latin squares in precisely the two disjoint isotopy orbits of sizes 6 and 50. An independently written bit-mask enumeration of all partial transversals gives 508 faces including empty and nonempty f-vector (25,150,250,79,3). Independent staged vertex matching has 226 pairs and four critical edges/52 critical triangles; a topological sort of all 1,406 signed face incidences proves acyclicity. The signed integral Morse boundary Z^52→Z^4 has Smith factors (1,1,1,1), giving reduced H2=Z^48 without torsion. Separately, an independently reconstructed edge-path presentation has 126 non-tree generators and 250 triangular relators; exact Tietze single-occurrence elimination removes all 126 and all relators, proving π1=1. The resulting connected 2-complex has no homology outside H2 and is simply connected, so Hurewicz plus homology Whitehead gives wedge_48 S². Isotopies preserve all faces, making the finite proof exhaustive for precisely the noncyclic order-five class. No inference for larger orders or equivariant homotopy.

In particular, the 2026 general Latin-square-graph clique-homology theorem is mathematically distinct: partial transversals are cliques of the complement of the Latin-square graph, not cliques of that graph.

value.rationale: Only two order-five isotopy classes exist. Determining the second class completes a natural finite topological classification of an intrinsically defined rainbow-matching/partial-transversal complex, with π1 and integral homotopy rather than merely face counts or Betti ranks. A topologist studying small Latin-square assignment complexes could use this exact missing case to test larger-order conjectures and distinguish the two isotopy types. The finite cutoff is canonical, not an arbitrary slice; no new infinite-family theorem is claimed.

final_claim: For either representative of the unique noncyclic order-5 isotopy class, the partial-transversal complex with cells as vertices and at-most-one-per-row,column,symbol faces has integral homotopy type wedge of 48 two-spheres; the cyclic class is prior work.
limitations: No claim of homotopy for Latin squares of higher order, and no equivariant classification.
Although exact and independently reconstructed, finite certificate does not establish originality; separate primary source comparisons and residual risk apply.
